bug_semantics: On --restore, hashcat reads argc/argv from a binary restore file and re-parses them with the full option table (user_options_getopt; originally getopt_long) after discarding the user's typed command line. There is no allowlist or denylist, so a crafted restore file can inject output-redirecting options such as --outfile/--outfile-format and --potfile-path. With a guaranteed-crack hash+wordlist pair, cracked plaintext is appended to an attacker-chosen writable path (e.g. ~/.bashrc), yielding arbitrary file write and follow-on command execution. CWE-88. CVE.org PUBLISHED, affected through 7.1.2; GitHub advisory not withdrawn.
flaw_origin: The unrestricted restore-argv replacement and second-pass option parse were first written in the public-history root of hashcat/hashcat (also tagged v2.00): src/oclHashcat.c does read_restore(), then myargc/myargv = rd->argc/rd->argv, then getopt_long(myargc, myargv, ...) including --outfile; src/shared.c read_restore() copies each restore-file argument via mystrdup with no option filtering. Later restore.c extraction and user_options_getopt refactors preserved that mechanism through v7.1.2 src/restore.c:364-368.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-68766 is a published CWE-88 argument-injection in restore-file option parsing, confirmed by the GHSA, VulnCheck advisory, and hashcat#4738 PoC, and accepted by upstream in fcae69f. The sink at v7.1.2 is restore_ctx_init resetting options and calling user_options_getopt on rd->argc/rd->argv with no restriction, so attacker-controlled restore argv can set --outfile/--potfile-path (and later --bridge-parameter1) and write attacker plaintext into arbitrary files. Line-history of that sink is a chain of moves/renames/parameter refactors, not new mechanism: user_options_getopt is the extracted form of the 2015 second-pass getopt_long on myargv after myargv was replaced from the restore file. The BIC is therefore the smallest surviving public first-write of that replacement+reparse: root 5065474b (v2.00). Parent-tree verification: the commit has no parent (introducer_parent_absent). It is an import-sized root, but no finer public member exists in this full-history clone or in the renamed oclHashcat GitHub URL, so per protocol it is a valid BIC rather than a decomposable squash. --restore-file-path (2016) and later dangerous options expand delivery/impact but do not first write the unrestricted parse. AI is judged only on that BIC object: human author/committer Jens Steube, no commit-object AI marker, so NOT_AI. Fix SHA is the direct non-merge patch fcae69f, which lands after v7.1.2 as required by the CVE range.
